subject: Bayesian Mediation Analysis With Latent Variables

messages.author: f767f57fb3113a98
messages.subject: Bayesian Mediation Analysis With Latent Variables
parts:
Dear list members,

I wonder whether I could run a mediation Analysis including latent variables in blavaan, such as it is easily implemented with lavaan :
library(lavaan)
  model <- '
   # latent variables
     X =~ x1 + x2 + x3
     M =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
     Y =~ y5 + y6 + y7 + y8
   
  fit <- sem(model,data=PoliticalDemocracy)
  summary(fit)
  
  model <- ' # direct effect
             Y ~ c*X
           # mediator
             M ~ a*X
             Y ~ b*M
           # indirect effect (a*b)
             ab := a*b
           # total effect
             total := c + (a*b)
         '
  fit <- sem(model, data = PoliticalDemocracy)
  summary(fit)

P.D. I think one option in the Bayesian context would be the R2OpenBUGS package:
https://psycnet.apa.org/record/2019-78964-001

However, it would be nice to know whether I could use blavaan for the same analysis. 

Thanks in advance and the best regards,

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Bayesian Mediation Analysis With Latent Variables
parts:
Yes, you can directly estimate this in blavaan, and no need to use boostrap or monte-carlo method. The inference from the posterior for the indirect effects have no assumption on its distribution

Not sure why you have 2 syntaxes called model, you only need 1

library(blavaan)

model <- '
   # latent variables
     X =~ x1 + x2 + x3
     M =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
     Y =~ y5 + y6 + y7 + y8

# direct effect
             Y ~ c*X
           # mediator
             M ~ a*X
             Y ~ b*M
           # indirect effect (a*b)
             ab := a*b
           # total effect
             total := c + (a*b)
         '

fit <- bsem(model, data = PoliticalDemocracy, std.lv=T)
  summary(fit)
